big: Rohan's father is 70. The FD pays less than he would like, but he lived through a market crash once and swore never again. Two kinds of fund try to sit in that gap.

lines: My father is 70. He wants better than an FD but cannot take big falls. What can he hold?
Two funds fit. Their tax and their risk are different, so let us open both and look inside.

alt: Two bars: a conservative hybrid with a small equity slice and an equity savings fund with equity, arbitrage and debt
caps: A conservative hybrid is mostly debt, with a small slice of equity as the kicker. Here equity is 15%.
An equity savings fund holds three things: equity, arbitrage and debt. This split is an example.
Equity plus arbitrage here is 67%, above the 65% line, so it is taxed as an equity fund.
The conservative hybrid's gains are generally taxed at slab rate, like a debt fund.

h: A good year and a bad year
alt: Bars comparing an equity fund and a conservative hybrid in a made-up bad year and good year
caps: Made-up years. In the bad year, equity falls 30% and the debt part slips 1%.
The equity fund loses 30%. The conservative hybrid loses about 5.4%, so ₹10 lakh shows ₹9.5 lakh.
In the good year equity gains 25% and debt 7%. The hybrid gains about 9.7%.
Small falls, not zero falls. And a smaller gain is the price of that calm.

title: Fair claims, and unfair ones
stops: Equity savings: 65% equity plus arbitrage gets equity tax
Conservative hybrid gains are generally at slab rate
The debt part carries no credit risk
alt: A shield with fair and unfair claims about equity savings and conservative hybrids
caps: Equity savings gets equity tax at 65% equity plus arbitrage. A conservative hybrid is generally at slab rate.
The debt part can still fall, through interest rate moves or a bond that defaults.
Expect steady, modest returns. Not spectacular, and not zero risk.

q: Rohan's father says he would be upset if ₹10 lakh ever showed below ₹9 lakh. In the film's bad year, which holding stays above that line?
opts: An aggressive hybrid with 70% equity, at about ₹7.9 lakh
A conservative hybrid with 15% equity, at about ₹9.5 lakh
An equity fund with every rupee in shares, at about ₹7 lakh
Every hybrid does, since all hold some debt to cushion falls
why: With 70% in equity, a 30% fall costs about 21%, leaving nearly ₹7.9 lakh, well below the line.
A 15% equity share loses about 5.4% in that year, so ₹10 lakh falls to about ₹9.5 lakh.
A full equity fund loses 30%, leaving ₹7 lakh. Calm funds exist because this fall is hard for some people.
Hybrids differ in equity share. A 70% equity hybrid still falls hard, so having some debt is not enough.

q: An equity savings fund holds 25% in equity, 42% in arbitrage and 33% in debt. The client assumes it is taxed like a debt fund because equity is only 25%. What is right?
opts: He is right, since the debt and equity shares fix the tax rate
Tax depends only on unhedged equity, which is 25% here
The investor chooses the tax status when buying the units
Equity plus arbitrage is 67%, so it gets equity-fund taxation
why: It looks right at first, but arbitrage is hedged equity and counts toward the 65% line, so the claim fails.
The test is equity and arbitrage together, not unhedged equity alone, so the 25% figure is the wrong base.
Tax status follows what the fund holds. The investor cannot choose it, whatever the plan or option.
The 65% line counts equity and arbitrage together, and 25% plus 42% is 67%, so equity taxation applies.

q: A conservative hybrid holds only 15% in equity, yet it fell more than expected after a bond in its debt portfolio was marked down. What did the buyer miss?
opts: The equity part was too small, so the fund could not recover
Conservative hybrids hold only government bonds, which cannot fall
The debt part has credit and rate risk, so check its quality
Funds with little equity cannot be hurt by anything but equity
why: A bigger equity share would have added risk. The fall came from the debt portfolio, not from too little equity.
Conservative hybrids may hold corporate bonds, and even government bonds change in price with rates.
A debt part can fall on a rate rise or a poor-quality bond. Checking its credit quality is part of choosing.
The debt part can lose value too. Calling the fund equity-only for risk purposes is a mistake.

q: The father's conservative hybrid gained 14% in a strong year. He now expects 14% every year. What should Rohan tell him?
opts: That was a strong equity year, so expect steady, modest gains
Expect 14% a year, since most of the fund sits in stable debt
Expect more than 14%, since a good year lifts the next year too
Expect exactly the same as an FD, since the fund is mostly debt
why: The equity kicker helped that year. In a typical year the debt base sets a steadier, more modest return.
Debt does not guarantee 14%. This year's return came from a strong equity run, which will not repeat on demand.
A good year does not lift the next one. Returns do not carry forward from year to year.
A conservative hybrid still holds some equity and may fall or rise differently from an FD, so it is not the same.

pts: Conservative hybrid: mostly debt, a small equity kicker, gains generally at slab rate.
Equity savings: equity, arbitrage and debt. Equity tax applies if the first two reach 65%.
Check the debt quality. Expect steady and modest, not zero risk.
